planting.note: Plant in fall or spring with roots shaded and top growth in sun; set the crown 2-3 inches below soil level to encourage resilient regrowth.

directions: A vigorous Clematis montana variant introduced from China in 1908, bearing masses of pure white four-sepaled flowers with distinctively broad, blunt tips and gracefully wavy edges, set off by golden stamens in late spring. Unlike most montana types it will sometimes produce a light second flush later in the season where climate allows. A pruning group 1 vine requiring no regular pruning beyond removing dead or overcrowded growth after flowering; excellent for scrambling over large arbors, fences, or into mature trees.

planting.note: Plant in well-drained, humus-rich soil with the crown set slightly below grade; provide netting or twiggy support for its slender, non-clinging stems.

directions: Raised in 1990 by Japanese breeder Kazushige Ozawa from a cross of the American natives Clematis crispa and Clematis viorna, 'Odoriba' bears small, slightly nodding bell-shaped flowers only about an inch across, intensely pink along the margins with a paler bar toward the base and yellow-green anthers. It is a free-flowering, long-blooming selection from midsummer into fall, classed in pruning group 3 (cut back hard in late winter) and best grown through a shrub or on a low trellis rather than a tall structure.

planting.note: Plant with the crown 2-3 inches below soil level in moist, well-drained soil; provide a trellis, shrub, or fence for support.

directions: A Swedish viticella selection named for the town of Sodertalje, producing abundant open, four- to six-sepaled flowers in reddish-pink with contrasting greenish-white stamens from midsummer into early autumn. Vigorous and reliably hardy, it is a pruning group 3 clematis, cut back hard to 12-18 inches in late winter each year to encourage fresh flowering growth. Well suited to scrambling through shrubs, over low walls, or along trellis and fence lines.

common_name: Clematis viticella 'Elly Elisabeth' (sprawling rosy-pink viticella clematis)

planting.note: Plant in full sun with the crown slightly below soil level; its lax, sprawling stems benefit from light twiggy support or being allowed to weave through neighboring shrubs.

directions: An unusual viticella selection that grows less like a climbing vine and more like a many-stemmed, sprawling border perennial, producing an abundance of small, clear rosy-pink nodding flowers from summer into fall. More vining than a true herbaceous Clematis integrifolia but far less clinging than typical viticella cultivars, it works well left to tumble over low supports or through adjacent shrubs. As pruning group 3, cut all growth back hard in late winter.

planting.note: Plant with the crown 2-3 inches below soil level in fertile, well-drained soil; give it a trellis, obelisk, or fence to climb.

directions: A vigorous viticella hybrid bearing rich violet-purple sepals centered by a contrasting white bar, with three-inch flowers produced in profusion from summer through fall. Reaching 10-15 feet in a season, it climbs readily by twining leaf stalks over trellises, arbors, or fences. A pruning group 3 clematis, cut all stems back to about a foot from the ground in late winter before new growth begins to keep plants floriferous and tidy.
